title: Cable cast-on
subtitle: A single-strand cast-on that works mid-row as well as at the start of a piece.
excerpt: The cable cast-on builds each new stitch by knitting between the last two stitches on the left needle. Firm, tidy, and useful for button bands and mid-row increases.
sourceNotes: Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), pp. 26-27. Weldon's Practical Knitter, Series 1 (1886).

glossaryTerms.definition: A cast-on method that builds stitches by knitting into the gap between the last two stitches on the left needle and slipping the new stitch back. Produces a firm, corded edge.

content.text: builds each stitch by inserting the right needle between the last two stitches on the left needle, wrapping the yarn, and slipping the new loop back. The edge it produces is firm and slightly corded, with a ridge on the right side that sits cleanly at a button band or pocket opening. Because it uses only the working yarn and no measured tail, it is the cleanest option for adding stitches mid-row. Difficulty: beginner.
Make a slip knot on the left needle (first stitch).
Knit into the slip knot but do not drop it. Slip the new loop back onto the left needle. Two stitches are now on the left needle.
For every subsequent stitch, insert the right needle between the first two stitches on the left needle (not into either stitch itself).
Wrap the yarn and draw a loop through to the front.
Slip that loop onto the left needle so it sits between the two stitches you just worked between.
Repeat steps 3-5 until you have the required number of stitches.

The cable cast-on appears wherever a pattern asks for stitches to be added mid-row: buttonhole completion, thumb gussets on mittens, and extra stitches for a neck shaping. It also suits any project where a firm decorative edge is wanted, such as the lower edge of a knitted cushion cover.

items.symptom: Stitches come out very tight and hard to work into
items.cause: Inserting the needle into a stitch rather than between stitches
items.fix: Aim for the gap between the two stitches on the left needle. If the stitches are close together, push the first stitch back slightly with the left thumb to open the gap.

items.cause: Pulling the new loop through too loosely before slipping back
items.fix: Snug each new stitch gently as it goes onto the left needle. A consistent, moderate pull matches the gauge of the cast-on stitches below.

items.symptom: Stitch count keeps growing unexpectedly mid-row
items.cause: Accidentally slipping the new stitch without dropping the old one
items.fix: After slipping the new stitch back, check that exactly one new stitch has been added. Count your stitches after every 10 cast-ons when learning.
